evidence_type: Author-supplied ModelViewer daylight close-up completing the requested tuned A/B views
observations: The focused Surface B material is displayed with the preferred hall settings and the green/Y-inverted hall bump texture.
Panel divisions, paint variation, dark glazing, transformer radiators and brown insulators remain readable, without the severe white clipping of the untuned close-ups.
Surface A and Surface B both look usable at the supplied daylight view. No decisive normal-direction advantage or new gross shading fault is evident in these screenshots.
limits: Camera framing shifts slightly from Surface A. Mode and displayed sun match, but this is a qualitative comparison rather than a registered pixel test.
The author's positive comment approves the visible Surface B appearance; it is not an explicit preference for B over A or proof of the renderer's required normal convention.
Only the hall controls are selected. All three material names are visible and the staged file matches the repository, but the screenshot is not a byte-level inspection of the viewer's memory.
Unseen angles, distance, full-plant assembly, dedicated night materials and gameplay remain unverified.

working_choice.reason: Use the positively reviewed Surface B as a reversible working choice for the next plant assembly, without claiming it outperformed A.
working_choice.fallback: Retain both tuned variants and the neutral-normal brightness reference for later diagnosis.

next_step: Carry the reviewed material approach into the complete plant with shared atlas reuse and appropriate facade variants; review appearance on that assembly rather than requesting another isolated-sample screenshot cycle.
evidence_storage: Unmodified screenshot archived locally outside Git; hashes and observations only are published.
